Resolves #18530

Turn the ordinary-pane ownership story into something the reader can run. `DockLayoutsPanes.md` now keeps its production-shaped five-file sequence as explained readonly context, then folds the same Model → Store → Provider → Controller → Grid → Workspace chain into one self-contained Portal live preview. The preview exposes the exact payoff: edit a record, move the live pane between groups, collapse it into a rail, reveal it, and pin it back without losing application state.

`DockLayoutsAdoption.md` now records the complementary verdict: its partial, app-local snippets remain readonly because executing them alone would teach a false boundary, and it links to the runnable ordinary-pane workspace.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge — the ownership story stops at a boundary the guide does not name, and I measured the other side of it today.**

The guide teaches pane ownership *within one workspace*: move the pane between groups, collapse it to a rail, reveal it, and the record and provider state survive. That is true and well demonstrated.

It is silent on what changes when a pane crosses into **another workspace** — the tear-out case — and that boundary has real enforced constraints rather than merely being out of scope. Item ids are unique across the whole keyed topology, so a pane cannot be *copied* into a second workspace, only moved; and a document that hands back its last pane is refused outright, because pruning its final tabs node leaves `root` dangling. I hit both while working on #18553 this morning, which is the only reason I can state them.

**Non-blocking, and I am not asking you to add it here** — this guide's scope is ordinary panes and widening it would blur exactly the teaching boundary you just made explicit. But a reader who finishes this guide has a mental model of "panes move freely and keep their state" that is correct inside one workspace and incomplete across two. Worth a successor ticket rather than a paragraph.

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit:**

- [x] PR description: framing matches what the diff substantiates — "the same ownership chain compressed into one executable module" is exactly what the fence contains, and the `readonly` rationale is a reason, not a hedge
- [x] Anchor & Echo summaries: N/A — no JSDoc surface
- [x] `[RETROSPECTIVE]` tag: N/A — none claimed
- [x] Linked anchors: `DockLayoutsAdoption.md`'s new paragraph cites the sibling guide as carrying the self-contained workspace, and it does

**Findings:** Pass. The prose claims are narrower than the evidence supports, which is the right direction.
